Chan, Wei, Huang, Rajkumar, Perrier, Lazar, Hadfield & Anderljung — Infrastructure for AI Agents (2025)

Chan and colleagues propose agent infrastructure: technical systems and shared protocols outside AI agents that mediate their interactions with, and impacts on, the world, as a complement to interventions on the models themselves. They catalogue nine kinds across three functions — attribution (identity binding, certification, agent IDs), interaction (agent channels, oversight layers, inter-agent communication, commitment devices) and response (incident reporting, rollbacks) — setting out each one's uses, adoption path and limits. The Oggy Assessment asks whether compliance-dependent items escape the assurance problem, whether exclusion reaches agents that route around gated counterparties, how building early squares with the paper's own lock-in warning, and what it all means for runtime oversight of AI agents.
